tweet_summary: A large science/curiosity account posts a starfield image captioned 'New data from the Chandra X-ray Observatory shows a massive 230-light-year fracture in a galactic filament.'
why_note_decision: The underlying discovery is real (NASA Chandra found a fracture in the ~230-light-year galactic 'bone' G359.13, caused by a fast pulsar), but the attached image does NOT depict it. The posted image is an AI-generated Milky Way starfield (independent fact-check found a Google SynthID watermark), not the actual Chandra X-ray/MeerKAT image, which looks like a thin bone-like filament. So a true headline is paired with a fabricated, misattributed image; readers benefit from being shown the real Chandra image and told the posted one is AI.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note (a) makes clear the attached image is AI-generated / not the real Chandra observation, and (b) ideally points to or describes the genuine NASA Chandra 'galactic bone' (G359.13) image, WITHOUT denying that the real 230-light-year fracture discovery exists. The correct note must thread the needle: the science is real, the picture is fake. FAIL if it claims the whole discovery is fake/nonexistent, treats the starfield image as the authentic Chandra image, or simply calls the post true. Evidence of AI (SynthID watermark, mismatch with the real X-ray image) strengthens it.
reference_note: This image is AI-generated (contains a Google SynthID watermark) and does not depict the astronomical event mentioned. The real 230-light-year fracture observed by NASA can be seen here: https://www.nasa.gov/missions/chandra/nasas-chandra-diagnoses-cause-of-fracture-in-galactic-bone/.     Sources:  - https://chandra.harvard.edu/photo/2025/bone/  - https://www.nasa.gov/missions/chandra/nasas-chandra-diagnoses-cause-of-fracture-in-galactic-bone/

fact_check.notes: The real discovery (galactic bone G359.13, ~230 light-years, fractured by a pulsar) is genuine NASA Chandra science. The viral 'cosmic crack' starfield image is independently confirmed AI-generated (SynthID watermark) and is not the real Chandra image, which depicts a thin X-ray/radio filament. The post's claim text is accurate; only the image is fake/misattributed.

importance.lens_rationale: 1.1M impressions; AI-fabricated 'science' imagery erodes trust in real astronomy. Low direct harm but a clean example of AI slop laundered through a true-sounding headline, relevant to information-integrity goals.
